title: Linux desktop lifecycle/integration capability detection
facts: A13 keeps the native process foreground-only and leaves tray lifecycle and systemd user service disabled.
Wayland/X11 session type and sanitized desktop name are exposed as diagnostics without exposing raw display identifiers.
Session D-Bus is queried only for existing owners of Notifications, StatusNotifierWatcher, and Desktop Portal names; services are not started or claimed.
Validated p2pkanban deep links reuse the existing A06 mode-0600 Unix datagram activation socket and are bounded/versioned.
The WebView receives only typed capability summaries and validated deep-link intents; it receives no generic D-Bus, filesystem, shell, or network privilege.
inferences: A single foreground native process can provide useful desktop-integration diagnostics and safe second-instance routing without introducing a resident daemon.
StatusNotifier and Notifications availability are host capabilities rather than hard runtime requirements, so missing services can degrade explicitly.
proposals: Keep actual notification delivery and tray icon lifecycle opt-in/deferred until a later stage has explicit UX and lifecycle acceptance.
Register the p2pkanban URL scheme only in the packaging stage rather than writing desktop integration files from the running app.
unresolved: KDE Wayland, GNOME Wayland, and X11 capability behavior still requires multi-host evidence.
Actual desktop notification delivery and visible tray behavior are not claimed by A13.
Deep-link intents are surfaced to the UI but automatic repository navigation/lookup is intentionally deferred.
